final_answer:
Quantum mechanics is a fundamental part of modern physics that emerged from the work of several key figures during its developmental history. The term "quantum mechanics" itself was coined by physicists Max Born, Werner Heisenberg, and Wolfgang Pauli in the early 1920s at the University of Göttingen. Their collective contributions laid significant groundwork for quantum theory's evolution.

Max Planck is often credited with starting this journey when he proposed his quantum hypothesis in 1900 to explain black-body radiation, which was a critical stepping stone towards developing quantum mechanics as we know it today. Albert Einstein furthered the field by introducing the concept of "photoelectric effect" for light quanta or photons and their role in energy transfer - an idea that challenged classical physics' understanding at the time.

Niels Bohr made significant contributions with his model of the atom, which incorporated quantum theory to explain atomic spectra – a major breakthrough during this era. Louis de Broglie proposed wave-particle duality for electrons and other particles - an essential concept in modern physics that has been instrumental since then.

Max Born's work on probability interpretation of the wave function, Werner Heisenberg’s matrix mechanics formulation which later evolved into his uncertainty principle – a cornerstone idea in quantum theory; Paul Dirac who unified relativity and quantum theories through his equation predicting antimatter - all these are key contributions to this field.

Erwin Schrödinger developed wave mechanics, another pillar of the modern understanding of quantum physics that complements Heisenberg's matrix formulation. Richard Feynman also made significant advances in Quantum Electrodynamics (QED), a theory describing how light and matter interact - an essential part of our current comprehension of quantum phenomena.

In summary, the development of quantum mechanics was not due to one single inventor but rather multiple scientists who contributed over time with their unique insights leading us towards this complex yet fascinating field in physics today.
